sentences.text:
The petitioners have filed this petition while praying for following reliefs :
i. Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to quash impugned order dated 30.11.2021 (Annexure P/5), in the interest of justice.

ii. Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to direct the respondent authorities to adjudicate the reference application (Annexure P/2) made by the petitioners within a time bound period, in the interest of justice.

iii. Any other relief which this Hon'ble Court may deem fit just and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case may kindly be issued in favour of the petitioner along with cost of the petition.

2. The facts as elaborated in the petition reflect that the petitioners who are agriculturist are resident of village Saavli and their land was sought to be acquired under the provisions of Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
The said proceedings ensued in passing of award dated 28.02.2013, the petitioners sought reference of the award by filing an application under Section 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

By impugned order dated 30.11.2021, the reference made by the petitioners under Section 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 has been dismissed, therefore, this petition is filed assailing the impugned order dated 30.11.2021.
3. Learned counsel for petitioners contends that in the present case, there is no order on merit by the Reference Court under Section 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
The Reference Court has dismissed the reference petition only on the ground that the same is time barred.

The counsel submits that in the present case, there is no order on merit by the Reference Court under Section 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 and the Reference Court failed to appreciate that the award was not passed in the presence of the petitioners and therefore, they were entitled to seek reference within a period of 6 months from the date of award.

It is further submitted that the award was passed on Ramvilas Rai vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84366523/
2 28.02.2013, a reference was sought by filing a reference petition on 13.08.2013 i.e. within a period of six months from the date of award.
4. It is contended by the counsel for the petitioners that the petitioners were never received any notice under Section 12 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 therefore, there was no occasion to file reference petition within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of notice under Section 12 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

State of Maharashtra & Ors.)
the counsel submits that the Reference Court be directed to take decision on the petitioners reference on merit.
5.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for respondents submits that the present petition is not maintainable inasmuch as, against an order passed under Section 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894, there is a remedy of appeal under Section 54 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
Therefore, in view of the existence of remedy under Section 54 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894, the present petition is not maintainable.

6. Learned counsel for respondents further submits that in the present case, the petitioners were issued notices under Section 12 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 and, therefore, as the notices were served upon the petitioners, the petitioners were required to seek reference under Section 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of notice under Section 12(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 .
It is contended that the notices under Section 12 was received prior to 28.02.2013.
Thus, submits that no interference is warranted.

7. Heard the rival submissions and perused the record.
8.
In the present case, the challenge is to an order of Reference Court under Section 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 dated 30.11.2021.
By the impugned order, the reference petition moved by the petitioners has been dismissed being barred by limitation.

A perusal of order dated 30.11.2021 which is contained in Annexure P/5 reflects that the order is not on merit and the Reference Court has been declined to entertain the reference petition only on the ground that the same is barred by limitation.

Undisputedly, an order passed under Section 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 is appealable under Section 54 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 but in the present case, there is no order on merit under Section 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 by the Reference Court.
Therefore, it would not be conducive and proper to relegate the petitioners to avail the remedy of appeal under Section 54 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

In view of the law laid down by the High Court of Bombay in the case of Chandaba Vs. State of Maharashtra & Ors. (WP No.13332/2022), the High Court of Bombay in the case of Chandaba (supra) in almost identical facts directed the Reference Court to decide the reference case on merit.

sentences.text: 9. A perusal of the order impugned dated 30.11.2021 reflects that the Reference Court has concluded that as the present petitioners derived the knowledge of passing of award dated 17.06.2013 i.e. the date on which they received certified copy of the award, they were required to file a reference petition within a period of six weeks from 17.06.2013 but the petitioners moved a reference petition on 13.08.2013 i.e. beyond the period of six weeks from 17.06.2013
therefore, the reference petition was time barred.

10. To deal with the order impugned, the provisions of Section 12 as well as Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 are reproduced herein :
12. Award of Collector when to be final .(1) Such award shall be filed in the Collectors office and shall, except as hereinafter provided, be final and conclusive evidence, as between the Collector and the persons interested, whether they have respectively appeared before the Collector or not, of the true area and value of the land, and the apportionment of the compensation among the persons interested.
(2) The Collector shall give immediate notice of his award to such of the persons interested as are not present personally or by their representatives when the award is made.
18. Reference to Court .(1) Any person interested who has not accepted the award may, by written application to the Collector, require that the matter be referred by the Collector for the determination of the Court, whether his objection be to the measurement of the land, the amount of the compensation, the persons to whom it is payable, or the apportionment of the compensation among the persons interested.

(2) The application shall state the grounds on which objection to the award is taken:
Provided that every such application shall be made,
(a) if the person making it was present or represented before the Collector at the time when he made his award, within six weeks from the date of the Collectors award;
(b) in other cases, within six weeks of the receipt of the notice from the Collector under section 12, sub-section (2), or within six months from the date of the Collectors award, whichever period shall first expire.
11.

A perusal of Section 12 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 reflects that an award which has been passed under Section 11 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 is required to be filed in the Collector Office and is treated to be final and conclusive evidence.
The notice of such award is required to be given to the person interest who are not present personally or by their representative when the award is made.

sentences.text: Section 18(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 provides that if a person is present at the time of making of award, he is required to seek reference within a period of six weeks from the date of award.

Section 2(b) of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 provides that when the person is not present at the time of passing of award, he is required to seek reference of the award within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of notice from the Collector under Section 12(2) of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 or within six months from the date of award of Collector whichever period shall expire earlier.
13. In the present case, there are specific averments by the petitioners in paragraph 6.4 of the petition that the petitioners were present when the award was passed.
The petitioners also before the Reference Court submitted vide Annexure P/4 that the petitioners were not given any opportunity of hearing before passing of award dated 28.02.2013.
The petitioners also made specific averments that they did not receive any notice under Section 12 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
The respondents before the Reference Court moved a reply to the Reference Petition which is contained in Annexure P/3.

In paragraph 2 of the reply, the respondents submitted as under :

14 . In paragraph 2 of the above, the respondents submitted that the notice under Section 12 Land Acquisition Act, 1894 was served upon the petitioners before 28.02.2013 (i.e. the date of award).
The paragraph 2 of the reply of the respondents, goes contrary to the provisions of Section 12(2) of Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
The notice under Section 12(2) of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 is required to be issued by the Collector when the award is already passed.
The provision does not stipulate any eventuality of issuing notice before passing of any award.

15. In terms of Section 12(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, the Collector was required to give notice after passing of award to the petitioners but in the present case, there is no document to establish that any notices issued to the petitioners under Section 12(2) of Land Acquisition Act,
1894.

The petitioners categorically submitted in paragraph 33 of the reference petition that they received a certified copy of the award on 17.06.2013 and 17.06.2013 is the date which has also been held to be the cut off date by the Reference Court on which the petitioners came to know about the passing of award.

Thus, in the present case, in terms of Section 18(2)(b), the petitioners were required to seek reference within a period of six months from the date of award passed by the Collector and accordingly, the petitioners moved a reference petition on 13.08.2013 before expiry of six months therefore, the Reference Court was required to appreciate that in the present case, the provisions of second part of Section 18(2)(b) of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 were applicable and not the provisions of first part.

16. Thus, in the considered view of this Court, the reference petition moved by the petitioners before the Reference Court was within the period of limitation having been preferred within a period of six months from the date of award.
Accordingly, in the peculiar circumstances of the case, the present petition is being entertained and accordingly order dated 30.11.2021 passed by the Reference Court is set aside.

The matter is remitted back to the Reference Court to take decision on reference petition Ramvilas Rai vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84366523/
5 on merit while extending opportunity of hearing to all concerned as expeditiously as possible preferably within a period of one year from the date of submission of certified copy of this order.
